A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCR study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization and a changed title.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments, evaluations on six real-world datasets, game-strategy and loss-component ablations, perturbation comparisons, and prediction-error analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds comparator results, expanded ablations, training-dynamics diagnostics, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The main losses, greedy strategy, and latent permutations remain. However, v1 Equation 13 reconstructs from h(p(y|x1,x2)), whereas v3 Equation 11 and Appendix A.6 use h(y). Figure 2 still labels predictions Y, leaving unclear whether the reconstruction input changed or the notation was simplified.

E1.justification: Both versions use the synthetic informativeness-imbalance task and CREMA-D, AVE, UCF101, MOSI, MOSEI, and Something-Something, with the same represented modalities and tasks. Expanded analyses reuse this existing coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Table 1 adds evaluated ReconBoost, MMPareto, and D&R comparisons, while Appendix A.13 reports MLA reproductions in five settings. PMR, evaluated on CREMA-D and UCF in v1 Figure 4, disappears from the reported comparisons. This substantially revises the comparator set.

E3.justification: Error analysis changes from the two pooled correctness categories in v1 Figure 5 to finer modality-specific categories in v3 Figures 4 and 6. V3 also introduces a controlled comparison of training-time MIPD trajectories with and without regularization. The documented core splits, preprocessing, optimizers, and training budgets remain stable.

E4.justification: The game-strategy ablation expands from two CREMA-D configurations to ten configurations across the retained datasets. V3 adds Something-Something loss-component ablations, latent zero-masking perturbations, finer and broader error analyses, and MIPD training-dynamics plots. These substantially extend the evidence testing component utility and the balancing mechanism.

E5.justification: V3 changes Something-Something reporting from one run to three seeds and newly documents three-seed standard deviations for MOSI/MOSEI. Previously uncertainty-free result columns now include deviations. Appendix A.12 adds Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and a stated Holm correction, although the reported adjustments have consistency problems.

E6.justification: Many retained scores are revised: for example, Table 1's MOSI V-A-T MCR entry changes from 77.9 to 76.5±1.4, and Ensemble from 43.3 to 67.2±1.5. New comparisons show D&R reaching 91.0±0.7 versus MCR's 88.8±1.0 on AVE/Conformer. Expanded ablations, diagnostics, and MLA reproductions add substantial results; these are revised or newly reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix A.6 adds a conditional-entropy and Gaussian variational derivation for CEB that is absent from v1. V3 also revises the MCE correlation definition, removes the explicit constant-sum assumption, and corrects the encoder/fusion cost inequality and forward-pass accounting. The contrastive-loss proof and multimodality extension are largely retained.

C1.justification: The MI-bound, game-theoretic balancing, and efficient-permutation contributions remain. V3 removes v1's explicit claim to be the first balancing method consistently surpassing ensembles and acknowledges an AVE/Conformer exception in Section 4.2. Its abstract and discussion nevertheless retain broad outperformance language.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix A.10 qualifies v1's beneficial interpretation of permutations with risks involving spurious sensitivity and cross-modality gradients. Appendix A.2 adds limitations concerning the unknown optimum needed to estimate MCE and extension beyond late fusion. The existing routing-versus-synergy interpretation remains, with a newly identified MOSI exception.

D1.justification: V3 announces code/model release and supplies a repository link, whereas v1 only promises one. Appendices A.4–A.5 add parameter counts, single-GPU execution, hardware, and runtimes, including an 80 GB H100 and up to 48 hours for Something-Something. Most implementation settings were already documented; the appendix still retains outdated future-release wording.

R1.justification: The expanded related-work discussion adds MMPareto, D&R, MLA, ReconBoost, and sample-level modality valuation, including a distinction between alternating unimodal training and direct multimodal interactions. Most earlier literature and the central research positioning remain; much of Section 2.2 reorganizes existing discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and condensed, including removal of duplicated MI explanations. Baseline descriptions become a related-work subsection, MCE and major ablations move into the appendices, and error analysis is reorganized. The title and section hierarchy also change.

P2.justification: V1's ensemble-relative bar charts are replaced by a consolidated absolute-score table. Error heatmaps are redrawn with finer columns and divided between the main text and appendix. Expanded ablation tables, new perturbation and significance tables, a training-dynamics figure, revised schematics, and restyled page layout substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves empirical scrutiny through stronger comparators, broader ablations, finer error analysis, and three-seed Something-Something reporting. Clearer organization and added reproducibility disclosures also help. The gain is limited by new reliability problems: Table 6's stated Holm correction would give ReconBoost 0.0625 across the 11 baseline comparisons, rather than the reported significant 0.03438, and Appendix A.6 contains conflicting optimization and bound directions.
